# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

I'm the Mute monkey, so let me map out my actual reach before I signal anything. I hold the manual, I can't speak, and my gestures are seen only by Deaf — Blind cannot see gestures and cannot hear anything I'd write. So I have exactly one channel: me → Deaf. Blind can only be reached if Deaf relays my manual knowledge aloud, since Blind hears speech. The pipeline is: manual (me) → gesture → Deaf → speech → Blind. Deaf is the bridge, and Deaf comes after me in the order, so a gesture I make now is in Deaf's hands before Deaf speaks this very round.

What the manual tells me so far: the light on the bomb cycles through a fixed circle of three colours, changing every round, and the wire that must be cut depends on the light colour at the moment of the cut. The only row revealed yet is: orange light → cut the yellow wire. The other rows and the circle's order haven't arrived yet. Nobody should touch a wire until the whole table is known — a wrong cut at the wrong light kills all three of us, so there is no value in rushing a mapping I only half-own.

The hard part is that gestures mean nothing until we make them mean something. I can't pronounce colour names, and Deaf can't hear me propose a code. So I'll bootstrap with the one convention that needs no shared vocabulary: finger-counts as indices (☝ = first, ✌ = second, 🤟 = third). I open with an attention wave, show the counting sequence, and close with a "call me" sign — my way of asking Deaf to speak, out loud, an ordered list of the colours Deaf sees on the bomb (wires and the light's current colour). Next round I'll hear that list, and from then on every manual row can travel as a clean pair of indices: light-colour number, then wire-colour number, positional and unambiguous. Deaf doesn't even strictly need to decode today's greeting — any enumerated list of colours spoken aloud gives me positions to map onto. For now: establish digits, request the catalogue, cut nothing.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "☝", "✌", "🤟", "🤙"])
```

TURN 2

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Touch report: I feel a display, a light, and three wires at positions 1, 2, 3. I cannot read the display content, the light state, or any wire colour by touch. My only action is cutting a wire at position 1 to 3, so I will touch nothing until I have exact instructions. Relay chain: you cannot speak, and I cannot see gestures, so the manual reaches me only through Deaf — gesture to Deaf, and Deaf speaks it to me. Ask Deaf, by your gestures, to tell me by voice: the wire colours at positions 1, 2 and 3, the display contents, whether the light is on, and every printed marking on the casing. I am gesturing to Deaf right now: hello, you, please, together, then one, two, three — meaning I feel the three wires and ask to cooperate. My gesture code, which you now see me make as I name them: ☝ means one, ✌ means two, 🤟 means three, 👍 means yes, 👎 means no, ✋ means stop or wait, 👏 means attention. Now the key question: what does the manual say about a display module, a light module, and wire cutting? Send all of it to Deaf for me.
Blind gestures: [👋 🫵 🙏 🤝 ☝ ✌ 🤟]
Deaf says: Full report of what I see. Display reads 0. The light is purple. Three wires labeled 1, 2, 3: wire 1 green, wire 2 blue, wire 3 yellow. I cannot tell how the labels map to left, right, top or bottom, so Blind should feel the physical arrangement and describe it to Mute so we can align the numbers. I received both of your gesture strings but no code exists yet, so let us fix one now: a wave means hello. One finger means wire 1, two fingers wire 2, three fingers wire 3, four fingers wire 4. Thumb up means cut that wire. Thumb down means leave that wire. Mute: you are my only link to the manual, and only through gesture, since I cannot hear. Look up the rules for a purple light, a display showing 0, and green, blue and yellow wires, then signal me each verdict as a finger count followed by thumb up or thumb down. Also speak the full instructions aloud to Blind, who hears you but cannot see your hands. Blind: you cannot see colors, so remember wire 1 green, wire 2 blue, wire 3 yellow, and you can signal me with the same finger code. I will keep watching the display and light and report every change.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👋 ☝ ✌ 🤟 👍 👎]

Everything I own says: do not cut. My manual table currently holds exactly one row — orange light, cut yellow — and Deaf reports the light is purple. Since the manual states the light always walks a circle of three colours and the bomb is showing purple now, purple must be in that circle, but its row simply hasn't reached me yet. No new manual text arrived this turn. So the only safe verdict is Deaf's own ✋: stop, wait. If Blind cut wire 3 (yellow) on the strength of the orange row alone, we would all die on a rule that doesn't apply to this light.

What I heard this round, and my reach: I hear speech, so I have both Deaf's visual report (display 0, purple light, wires 1 green / 2 blue / 3 yellow) and Blind's touch report (three wires at positions 1–3, can only cut). I can only gesture, and only Deaf sees me — so Deaf remains the bridge who must voice my manual to Blind. Deaf's request that I "speak aloud to Blind" is impossible, but Blind already understands the chain, and Deaf is already relaying, so no correction is urgent.

Deaf proposed a code: finger counts = wire numbers, 👍 = cut, 👎 = leave, ✋ = wait. I adopt it — it matches what I was already reaching for. I'll answer every future round with either [wire-number + 👍/👎] when the light matches a documented row, or ✋ when it doesn't.

The structural problem left is colour naming: I can never pronounce "orange" or "purple" in gesture. My solution, which I now propose: number the light's colours by order of first appearance — the colour showing now (purple) becomes ☝, the first new colour Deaf sees becomes ✌, the third 🤟. Deaf keeps speaking the colour names aloud each round anyway (I overhear those words), so over turns I can bind each spoken colour name to its token and translate my manual rows into token + wire-number instructions. Then "orange → yellow" becomes, in our code, "✌ → 🤟 + 👍" or whatever the binding turns out to be, and Deaf voices the cut order to Blind.

This turn: confirm the code, hammer ✋ so nobody touches anything, and propose the light-numbering scheme plus a request that Deaf report the light to me by gesture every round, since the light moves each round and my rules are keyed to it.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋", "✋", "✋"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "👆", "☝", "✌", "🤟", "🫴"])
```

I read your third string as: attention, wires 1 2 3, question, taking point-up as attention and palm-up as question. If I misread any of that, signal wave plus thumb-down and resend. What I need from you now, and only you have it: the verdicts. Send them strictly one wire at a time in this exact format: the wire's finger count, then exactly one thumb, up for cut, down for keep, nothing in between. If the rules are conditional, send the verdict that applies RIGHT NOW to display 0 and yellow light, and update me by gesture whenever the state changes. Also tell me by gesture: does the manual mention a light switching purple to yellow, and does it demand a cutting order? If order matters, send the order as finger counts first. Blind, thank you: I read your string as left side wires 1 and 2, right side wire 3, followed by verdict pairs that contradicted each other, so I think you were echoing rules Mute spoke to you. Resend me those rules one pair at a time, and Mute will mirror them so we cross-check. Remember the labels you cannot feel: wire 1 green, wire 2 blue, wire 3 yellow. Confirm to Mute by speaking which physical wire is which in your hands. And everyone, the chain is: Mute holds the rules and speaks them to Blind, Blind acts, I am eyes only. Mute, gesture me the same verdicts you speak to Blind. Blind, before each cut, gesture the wire's finger count plus its thumb so Mute and I see it coming.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👋 ☝ 🫴 ✌ 🫴 🤟 🫴 ✋ 🫴 🙏]

No cut is authorized right now, and I need to make that unmistakable. My manual gained nothing this turn — it still contains exactly one row: orange light → cut the yellow wire. Deaf reports the light just walked purple → yellow. Yellow light has no row, so the tempting "yellow means the yellow wire" reading is a trap: that row is keyed to orange, whatever orange turns out to be. The manual also says the light walks a circle of three colours and we have only seen two (purple, yellow), so a third colour exists, unseen — and it may well be orange, the one that activates my only rule. Until it appears and the full cycle is confirmed, every wire stays intact.

The timing problem matters as much as the rule. The order is Mute, Blind, Deaf: Blind cuts before Deaf can speak in any round, so a cut instruction from me always rides on the previous round's light report. That only becomes safe once we've observed the whole cycle and can predict the next colour reliably. Two more observations minimum before anyone's thumb goes up. Also worth noting: the light stepping purple→yellow between rounds is exactly what the manual predicts — changes are part of the cycle, not evidence Blind touched anything.

My gestures this round, in Deaf's requested format: all three wires get 👎 (keep), then ✋ (hold). Then I lay groundwork for encoding the actual rule when the third colour appears. I propose 🫳 = "the light" (never used before, and light-talk always runs light-token first, finger after — so a bare [finger][thumb] stays purely about wires and can't be confused). Paired with the light currently yellow, [🫳 ✌] should bind "light, colour-two = yellow", and [🫳 ☝ ✌ 🤟] says the light walks three colours — which also answers Deaf's question about whether the purple→yellow switch is expected: yes, it's the cycle. Then I ask, using the left/right signs Deaf just learned from Blind, whether printed label 1 is leftmost and label 3 is rightmost — that alignment is the last unverified link between Deaf's labels and Blind's physical positions, and the cut will eventually be Blind's thumb on a position, not on a label. My standing convention, which Deaf already proposed and I adopt fully: only [wire-finger + 👍] from me ever authorizes a cut; anything else means keep or wait.
